figures.finding: Iran's Civil Code fixes majority (bulugh) at fifteen full lunar (Hijri) years for a boy and nine for a girl (art. 1210), while most child-protection laws, the Protection of Children and Adolescents Act among them, treat everyone under eighteen as a child; a child leaves guardianship on reaching maturity (art. 1193).
figures.applies: Iran (the State's 2015 report; rushd, the separate test of financial maturity, not read).

sources.said: Article 1210 of the Iranian Civil Code states that: “The majority age for the boy is full 15 years according to the Hijri calendar and for the girl full 9 years according to the Hijri calendar.”
“Article 1193: As soon as a child reaches the age of maturity, he will cease to be under guardianship
All the persons who have not attained the age of 18 according to the Iranian calendar, shall benefit from the legal protections provided for by this Act.

sources.title: Islamic Republic of Iran: third and fourth periodic reports, CRC/C/IRN/3-4 (9 April 2015)
